                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XI.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p>NOW <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 11. 32. called Jephte.</ns0:note> Jephthah the Gileadite <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">So called, either from his Father <ns0:hi>Gilead, Ios.</ns0:hi> 17. 1, 2. or from the Mountain, or City of <ns0:hi>Gilead,</ns0:hi> the place of his birth or abode.</ns0:note> was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> a wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man an harlot</ns0:note> an harlot <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> A Bastard; for though such were not ordinarily <ns0:hi>to enter into the Congregation of the Lord, Deut.</ns0:hi> 23. 2. Yet God can dispence with his own Laws, and hath sometimes done honour to base-born persons, so far, that some of them were admitted to be the Progenitors of the Lord Jesus Christ.</ns0:note>: and Gilead <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">One of the Children of that An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cienter <ns0:hi>Gilead, Numb.</ns0:hi> 32. 1. <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> 17. 1.</ns0:note> begat Jephthah.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 And Gileads wife bare him sons, and his wives sons grew up, and they thrust out Jeph<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thah, and said unto him, Thou shalt not inherit in our fathers house, for thou <ns0:hi>art</ns0:hi> the son of a strange woman.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 Then Jephthah fled <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> from the face.</ns0:note> from his brethren, and dwelt in the land of Tob <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The name either of the Land or Territory, or of the Man who was the Owner or Ruler of it. This place was in or near <ns0:hi>Gilead,</ns0:hi> as appears by the speedy intercourse which here was between <ns0:hi>Iephthah</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Israelites.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>: and there were ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thered <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Judg. 9 4. 1 Sam. 22. 2.</ns0:note> vain men <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Idle per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons, who desire to get their living rather by Spoil and Ra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pine, than by honest and diligent Labour. These evil mind<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed persons <ns0:hi>Iephthah</ns0:hi> managed well, employing them against the Enemies of God, and of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> that bordered upon them; and particularly, upon Parties of the <ns0:hi>Ammonites,</ns0:hi> which made the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> more forward to chuse him for their Chieftain in this War.</ns0:note> to Jephthah, and went out with him <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">When he made excursions and at<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tempts upon his and their Enemies.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 ¶ And it came to pass <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> after days.</ns0:note> in process of time <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>after</ns0:hi> some <ns0:hi>days:</ns0:hi> or, <ns0:hi>after a year, days</ns0:hi> being oft put for a <ns0:hi>year,</ns0:hi> as hath been shewed; after that year mentio<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 10. 8. The <ns0:hi>Ammonites</ns0:hi> had vexed and oppressed them Eighteen Years, and now that the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> begin to make Opposition, they commence a War against them. Or, some time after <ns0:hi>Iephthah</ns0:hi> had been banish'd, and after he had taken up Arms, and given them some disturbance. Or, af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> assembled together, as is said, <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 10. 18.</ns0:note>, that the children of Ammon made war against Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And it was so, that when the children of Ammon made war against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">By direction or instinct from God, who both qualified him for, and called him to the office of a Judge. See <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 12. 7. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 11. 32. Otherwise they might not have chosen a Bastard, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32. 2. Unless we will say, that there being no other person among them fit for, and willing to this Work, necessity dispensed with this Law, as it did with other positive Laws, as those of the Sabbath and Sacrifices.</ns0:note> out of the land of Tob.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And they said unto Jephthah, Come and be our Captain <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">They say not, <ns0:hi>our King;</ns0:hi> for the experience of <ns0:hi>Abime<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lech's</ns0:hi> kingship had cooled their Appetite in that particular; but our Captain.</ns0:note>, that we may fight with the children of Ammon.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 And Jephthah said unto the elders of Gilead, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 26. 27.</ns0:note> Did not ye hate me, and expel me out of my fathers house <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">And deprive me of all share in my Fathers Goods, which, though a Bastard, was due to me. This Expulsion of him was the act of his Brethren; but he here ascribes it to the Elders of <ns0:hi>Gilead;</ns0:hi> either because some of them were among these Elders, as is very probable from the dignity of this Family; or because this act, though desired and pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />moted by his Brethren, was executed by the decree of the Elders, to whom the determination of all controversies about Inheritances belonged; and therefore it was their fault that they did not Protect him from the Injuries of his Brethren, as their duty was.</ns0:note>? and why are ye come unto me now, when ye are in distress?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And the Elders of Gilead said unto Jephthah, Therefore we turn again to thee now <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Being sensible that we have done thee Injury, we come now to make thee full Reparations.</ns0:note>, that thou mayest go with us, and fight against the children of Ammon, and be our head over all the inhabi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tants of Gilead.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 ¶ And Jephthah said unto the elders of Gilead, If ye bring me home again <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">If you recall me from this place where I am now set<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led, to the place whence I was Expelled.</ns0:note> to fight against the children of Ammon, and the LORD deliver them before me, shall I be your head <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Will you re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally make good this Promise? <ns0:hi>Iephthah</ns0:hi> was so sollicitous in this case, either from his Zeal for the publick Good, which required that he should be so; or from the Law of Self-Preservation, that he might secure himself from his Bre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thren; whose ill-will he had experienced, and whose in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />iuries he could not prevent, if, after he had served their ends, he had been reduced to his private capacity; or, there might be some Tincture of Ambition in him; for which God therefore severely, though paternally, chasti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />seth him, as we see afterwards.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:202" />10 ¶ And the elders of Gilead said unto Jeph<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thah, The LORD <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> be the hearer be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tween us.</ns0:note> be witness between us <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">They confirm their Promise by a Solemn and Sacred Oath.</ns0:note>, if we do not so according to thy words.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 Then Jephthah went with the elders of Gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lead, and the people made him head and captain over them: and Jephthah uttered all his words <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Objectively so called, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> All that was spoken, not onely by him, but also by the Elders of <ns0:hi>Gilead,</ns0:hi> con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning him, and concerning this whole Transaction, and the conditions of it; or, <ns0:hi>all his matters,</ns0:hi> the whole busi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness.</ns0:note> before the LORD <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Before the Publick Congregation, wherewith God was usually, and then especially present; see <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 20. 24. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 6. 25. <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 18. 10. Or, before the Altar, which possibly they did erect upon this special occasion, by Gods Permission: Or, in Gods Presence, calling him to be present, as a Witness and Judge between them.</ns0:note> in Mizpeh.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 ¶ And Jephthah sent messengers <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Ambassadors, to prevent Blood-shed, and make Peace; as far as in him lay; that so the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> might be acquitted before God and men from all the sad conse<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quences of this War; Herein he shewed great Prudence, and no less Piety.</ns0:note> unto the king of the children of Ammon, saying, What hast thou to do with me <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">What pretence, or reasonable cause hast thou for this Invasion?</ns0:note>, that thou art come against me, to fight in my land <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">He speaks this in the Name of all the People, whose the Land was.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And the king of the children of Ammon an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swered unto the messengers of Jephthah, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Numb. 21. 13.</ns0:note> Because Israel took away my land <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> This Land of <ns0:hi>Gilead,</ns0:hi> which was mine, but unjust<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly taken from me, by <ns0:hi>Sihon</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Og,</ns0:hi> the Kings of the <ns0:hi>Amo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rites;</ns0:hi> and the injury perpetuated by <ns0:hi>Israel's</ns0:hi> detaining it from me.                   <ns0:p n="14">14 And Jephthah sent messengers again unto the king of the children of Ammon.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And said unto him, Thus saith Jephthah, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 2. 9.</ns0:note> Israel took not away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 But when Israel came up from Egypt, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 14. 25.</ns0:note> walked through the wilderness unto the red-sea <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Unto which they came three times; once, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 13. 18. again, a little after their passage over it, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 15. 22. and a third time, long after, when they came to <ns0:hi>Ezion-Gaber, Numb.</ns0:hi> 33. 35. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 2. 8. which was upon the Shoar of the Red-Sea, 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 9. 26. 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 8. 17. from whence they went to <ns0:hi>Kadesh, Numb.</ns0:hi> 20. of this time he speaks here.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 20. 1.</ns0:note> came to Kadesh:</ns0:p>
